newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says differences remain on NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says differences remain on NATO expansion.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Sunday differences remained with the United States' European partners over which countries should be asked to join NATO this summer but he did not believe this would damage the alliance.

"We still have differences of opinion about whether in the first round there should be three or five nations admitted -- or some favor four -- but I do not expect it to do lasting damage to the alliance," he told a news conference after a Group of Seven summit.

Clinton, who discussed the issue in meetings with European leaders here, announced on June 12 he backed inviting just Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic when NATO leaders make their final choice at a summit in Madrid on July 8. "I'm confident our position is the prudent, the disciplined and the right one," he said.

France has strongly backed Romania to join in this first post-Cold War wave of NATO expansion and Italy strongly backs Slovenia. Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said here Clinton was making "a big mistake".
Clinton said it was important to maintain "an open door" to other countries to join later and there should be "an extra outreach" to countries seen as likely next-round entrants.

Of Romania and Slovenia, he said: "I believe that they are excellent candidates for admission in NATO membership if they stay on the path of reform and they continue to build up their partnership with us militarily..."
